A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RestoreVAR work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. V2 ends after its references despite referring to supplementary material; v3 includes Appendices A–K. The supplied documents support reliable comparison of what each version reports.

before.justification: V2 reports original restoration experiments, generalization evaluations, component ablations and a user study covering 50 scenes with 36 responses (Section 4, Tables 1–4).

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and reports additional sampling, component, perceptual-quality and failure-case evaluations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same degraded-latent cross-attention, RoPE, AdaLN removal, latent refiner transformer and continuous-latent decoder fine-tuning, with unchanged objectives and inference procedure. Appendix F supplies architectural specifications without establishing a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix J adds a severe low-light example from SID (Figure 25), extending the tested input conditions. The five restoration tasks and eleven datasets listed in Section 4.2 are unchanged; most additional appendix evaluations use this retained coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Diff-Plugin, AutoDIR and PixWizard to the generalization comparison, which previously included only five non-generative competitors. Although these LDM methods already appeared in Table 1, their participation in this corresponding comparison is new. The original Table 1 comparator set and exclusion of AutoDIR's structure correction module are retained.

E3.justification: Existing training budgets and dataset splits remain unchanged, but v3 substantially expands evaluation procedures. Appendix B adds a DDIM sweep over 50, 40, 30, 20, 10, 5 and 2 steps; Appendix D.1 compares positional embeddings after ten epochs at 512×512; Appendix E.3 adds MUSIQ/CLIPIQA evaluation to the Table 1 benchmarks. Appendices D.4 and I introduce altered-input component controls.

E4.justification: V3 retains the original conditioning, discriminator and refiner ablations while adding several distinct investigations: scale replacement in restored outputs, real-world scale decomposition, APE versus RoPE, decoder loss removal, LRT perceptual quality and restoration independence, and AutoDIR's dependence on its LDM output. Appendix J also supplies an explicit severe-degradation failure case.

E5.justification: V2 reports point estimates without confidence intervals or significance tests. Appendix E and Tables 7–8 newly report 95% confidence intervals, paired t-tests and Wilcoxon analyses for the retained user study and generalization results, including dataset-weighted per-image comparisons. The study still has 36 responses; no increase in training runs or seeds is established.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 3 and 4 and the existing Table 2 rows retain their values. Substantial results are added: Table 2 now reports AutoDIR's average MUSIQ/CLIPIQA as 56.767/0.386 versus RestoreVAR's retained 56.217/0.383. V3 also supplies DDIM speed-quality curves, Table 9 perceptual scores, and additional component and failure findings. These are newly reported results, not same-setting improvements over v2's RestoreVAR scores.

T1.justification: V2 asserts an O(log n) complexity advantage but does not include its referenced derivation. Appendix C introduces geometric-scale and quadratic-attention assumptions and derives O(n^4) versus O(n^4 log n) costs for equal numbers of forward steps. This is a substantial formal addition, although the printed closed-form sum and ratio contain algebraic inconsistencies.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: the first VAR-based generative AiOR framework, improved generative restoration performance, over tenfold faster inference and strong generalization. The additional evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly attributes slightly weaker generalization metrics than LDM competitors to smaller backbone pretraining. Additional discussion interprets the LRT's negligible perceptual impact and assigns primary restoration responsibility to VAR using component controls. Appendix J extends v2's decoder limitation with an LRT/decoder quality ceiling and an explicit severe-low-light failure boundary.

D1.justification: Appendix F supplies embedding dimensions, attention-head counts, latent resolutions, gated SOS construction and the LRT's twelve-block configuration. Appendices E, G and H add survey instructions, component runtime/parameter accounting and identification of RESIDE for the refiner evaluation. The new reproducibility statement promises code after review; it does not establish a current release. Existing optimizer, GPU and loss-weight disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 changes PixWizard's backbone attribution from SD-XL to Lumina-next, replacing the associated citation. V3 adds references for SID, ImageNet, DDIM and consistency distillation, alongside a short discussion of consistency and rectified-flow approaches. Positioning against VarSR, Varformer and the main restoration literature remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The original main-section order and most wording are retained. Edits include localized expansion of Sections 4.3–4.4, renaming the ablation heading, adding ethics and reproducibility statements, and updating affiliation/header text. A structured supplementary roadmap accompanies the appended material, without extensive rewriting of the original narrative.

P2.justification: V3 adds statistical and computational tables, sampling and positional-embedding plots, architecture diagrams, survey screenshots and extensive qualitative panels. Table 2 gains generative rows and a caption restricting bold highlighting to RestoreVAR and non-generative methods. Existing Figures 2 and 6–8 are relocated; Figure 12 extends the earlier discriminator illustration with additional loss-ablation columns.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses important evidential gaps by including LDM competitors in the generalization comparison, testing the speed advantage against DDIM acceleration, and supplying architecture and ablation material only referenced in v2. These additions substantially improve assessment of the central efficiency, fidelity and generalization tradeoffs; statistical reporting and failure cases further clarify reliability and applicability. Appendix C's algebraic inconsistencies and unclear parameter accounting in Tables 5 and 10 limit those additions, but the empirical controls and reproducibility gains provide a clear substantial net improvement.
